static_traits.name: Lin Nan
static_traits.family_status: No immediate family members, living alone
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with friends affected by fear of failure and avoiding activities; has two good friends but has not yet discussed feelings of failure and disappointment with them
static_traits.medical_history: No past counseling or therapy history, no major physical illness; no similar problems in the past
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, can describe emotions and experiences and cooperates with recording automatic thoughts; logic fairly coherent but tending toward catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking; cautious and skeptical about change but willing to try

basic_info.main_problem: After losing a recent billiards competition, feeling one should not play again, developing feelings of failure and disappointment that gradually escalate; starting to avoid billiards and other activities, distancing from friends, fearing failure; such feelings appear whenever facing setbacks.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to recognize and change catastrophic reactions and black-and-white beliefs about setbacks, challenge negative beliefs, and recover enjoyment of activities.

core_beliefs: My self-worth depends on winning/losing and performance

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot win, it means I am no good and should not play again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids playing pool again to avoid failure and embarrassment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should never play billiards again

special_situations.event: Considering whether to try playing pool again
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot ensure success, trying again will only prove I am no good and humiliate me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding any activity not certain to succeed
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will lose again; this will prove I am no good, and it is embarrassing

special_situations.event: Friends' invitations or social event settings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I perform poorly in front of friends, they will look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding meeting friends and joining activities
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am terrible; best not to go

special_situations.event: Increased work stress, not yet reaching self-set high standards
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach my own high expectations, it equals personal failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces engagement and enthusiasm; avoids challenges to reduce the risk of failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have done better; not doing so means failure

core_conflict.wish: Longing to gain self-worth and recognition through good performance and victory
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure triggering shame and being devalued and judged by others
defense_goal: Avoiding failure and shame by avoiding attempts and maintaining high control standards, protecting self-esteem

object_relations.self_representation: A 'not-good-enough person' easily defined by failure
object_relations.object_representation: Others/audiences who may judge and belittle oneself at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to try activities with a possible risk of failure, or encouraged in counseling to challenge negative beliefs and conduct behavioral experiments
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If she tries she will fail and be humiliated, so avoidance is a safer choice (transference: seeing others as potential judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a tactful, cautious tone, emphasizing 'safety' and 'lack of confidence', offering many reasons to justify not trying or postponing, reducing explicit commitments.

manifestations: Avoids activities and friends for fear of failure
Not yet discussed feelings of failure and disappointment with close friends
Constrains oneself with 'must / should'-style high expectations
Choosing not to try when success is uncertain, seeking 'safety'
outcomes: Declining enjoyment and enthusiasm for life

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Defining self-worth by winning/losing and perfection standards

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the behavioral impulse they originally wanted to act outwardly, turns to act on themselves, and converts the energy inward, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Knowing activities bring joy yet choosing not to participate, turning energy into self-doubt and self-criticism
Avoids trying to reduce the shame of potential failure

positive_force: Realizes catastrophic thinking and proactively seeks counseling help
Willing to try recording and observing automatic thoughts
Work performance basically not yet affected, still with stable occupational functioning
Has two friends to talk with (potential support resources)
negative_force: Significant catastrophic and black-and-white cognitive patterns
Tightly binding self-worth with winning/losing and performance
Intense shame about failure and anticipatory worry lead to avoidance
Social withdrawal and activity avoidance, declining enthusiasm

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding activities and social situations where failure is possible (including no longer playing billiards, reducing interaction with friends)
antecedent: Thinking about possible failure or poor performance
Friends inviting to participate in activities
Increased work stress, not yet reaching self-set high standards
target_behavior.core_reason: Tying self-worth to winning and losing, catastrophizing predictions about failure accompanied by feelings of shame
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential failure and embarrassment, protecting self-esteem and reducing anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Declining interests and enthusiasm, damaged social relationships, increased self-doubt, reduced enjoyment of life

target_behavior.behavior: Extreme verbal and cognitive expressions after setbacks (e.g. 'I will never play billiards again') accompanied by anxiety
antecedent: Experiencing failure or not yet meeting expectations
Facing tasks not certain to succeed
target_behavior.core_reason: Black-and-white thinking and catastrophizing tendencies, self-denial triggered by high expectations
target_behavior.function: Gaining a sense of control through extremized conclusions, avoiding the anxiety brought by trying again
target_behavior.consequence: The problem is solidified, reducing opportunities for practice and improvement, and intensifying disappointment and withdrawal
